newsitem.title: CHINA: China Hainan Airlines to buy 7 Boeing 737, 3 767s.
newsitem.headline: China Hainan Airlines to buy 7 Boeing 737, 3 767s.

text.p: China's Hainan Airlines plans to buy seven 737s and three 767 aircraft from Boeing Corp over the next two years, company officials said on Wednesday.

The regional airline, based in the southern tropical island province of Hainan, has already agreed on a basic contract with the U.S. planemaker for four 737-400s and three 737-800s, airline Chairman and President Chen Feng told Reuters.
Hainan Airlines was awaiting final approval from China's aviation authorities to buy three Boeing 767 aircraft for about $60-70 million each.

Delivery of the Boeing 737s and 767s was expected to begin in 1998, when Hainan Airlines also plans to bring into operation seven Metro-23 light aircraft bought from U.S. manufacturer Fairchild Aircraft Inc, Chen said.
"Next year, we plan to take about 20 aircraft," Chen said. "It's big money... minimum $600 million."

The airline, which currently operates just nine Boeing 737s and a handful of turboprops and executive jets, plans to take out options on a further three 737-800s in addition to the initial purchases, said airline chief economist Li Bing.

Part of the cost of the new aircraft would be covered by the airline's planned issue of around 80 million foreign currency B shares to be listed on the Shanghai bourse in the first quarter of this year, company officials said.
Chen said a bond issue in the United States worth around $300 million was also planned.

The airline, which is 25 percent owned by American Aviation Investment, a fund partially controlled by U.S. financier George Soros, is expected to become the first airline to list publicly on China's domestic exchanges.
